sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: With a single monumental action expected today, the Trump administration will eliminate its own legal authority to fight climate change.
sentences.zh: 随着今天预计将采取的一项具有划时代意义的单一行动，特朗普政府将消除其自身打击气候变化的法律权力。

sentences.en: My colleague, Lisa Friedman, has spent the past few weeks piecing together the inside story of how a small group of activists turned that once improbable goal into reality.
sentences.zh: 我的同事莉萨·弗里德曼花了几周时间，拼凑出了一则内幕故事，讲述了一小群积极分子是如何将那个曾经看似不可能实现的目标变成现实的。

sentences.en: Thursday, February 12th.
sentences.zh: 2月12日，星期四。

sentences.en: Lisa, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 莉萨，欢迎回到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: So over the summer, Lisa, you broke the story that the Trump administration was planning to roll back the legal basis
sentences.zh: 所以在夏天，莉萨，你爆料称特朗普政府正计划收回法律依据，

sentences.en: for the entire government's ability to regulate greenhouse gases.
sentences.zh: 即整个政府监管温室气体的能力。

sentences.en: Just remind us what that legal basis was and why its elimination would be so consequential.
sentences.zh: 请提醒我们，那个法律依据是什么，以及为什么废除它会产生如此深远的影响。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It's called the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 这被称为危害认定。

sentences.en: And you can think of it like the spine of America's ability to regulate climate pollutants.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成美国监管气候污染物能力的脊梁。

sentences.en: Congress never explicitly told the EPA that it could regulate planet warming emissions.
sentences.zh: 国会从未明确告诉环保署它可以监管地球变暖排放。

sentences.en: But in 2007, the Supreme Court ruled in a landmark ruling, it's called Massachusetts v.
sentences.zh: 但在2007年，最高法院作出了一项具有里程碑意义的裁决，被称为马萨诸塞州诉

sentences.en: EPA, that greenhouse gases qualify as pollutants under the law.
sentences.zh: 环保署案，裁定温室气体根据法律符合污染物的标准。

sentences.en: And because EPA is required to set limits, required to regulate damaging pollutants, the court told the agency, you need to determine whether these greenhouse gases,
sentences.zh: 由于环保署被要求设定限制、被要求监管破坏性污染物，法院告诉该机构，你需要确定这些温室气体——

sentences.en: carbon dioxide, methane, others, whether they endanger health and welfare.
sentences.zh: 二氧化碳、甲烷以及其他气体——是否危害健康和福利。

sentences.en: Two years later, the EPA, citing a massive body of scientific evidence, came out with what is now called the endangerment finding,
sentences.zh: 两年后，环保署援引了大量的科学证据，发布了现在被称为危害认定的文件，

sentences.en: that six greenhouse gases do pose a danger to public health and the environment.
sentences.zh: 即六种温室气体确实对公众健康和环境构成了危害。

sentences.en: And therefore should be regulated.
sentences.zh: 因此应该受到监管。

sentences.en: And therefore should be regulated.
sentences.zh: 因此应该受到监管。

sentences.en: So if you think of the endangerment finding as the spine, that is what has allowed for regulations on carbon emissions from automobiles, from power plant smokestacks,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你把危害认定视为脊梁，正是它允许对汽车碳排放、发电厂烟囱排放、

sentences.en: methane from oil and gas well leaks.
sentences.zh: 以及油气井泄漏的甲烷进行监管。

sentences.en: And if you repeal the endangerment finding as the Trump administration is about to do, then there is no basis, there is no legal basis or scientific basis
sentences.zh: 如果你像特朗普政府即将做的那样废除危害认定，那么在美国，监管温室气体排放就

sentences.en: for regulating greenhouse gas emissions in the United States.
sentences.zh: 没有任何依据，没有法律依据或科学依据。

sentences.en: The government essentially gives up its authority.
sentences.zh: 政府基本上放弃了其权力。

sentences.en: And not to mix metaphors, but when the endangerment finding goes away, all of these regulations that stem from it fall like a house of cards.
sentences.zh: 而且虽说不上混淆比喻，但当危害认定消失时，所有源于它的法规都会像纸牌屋一样倒塌。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And during our first conversation, when you first explained all this to our listeners, Lisa, you had told me that the efforts to eliminate the endangerment finding
sentences.zh: 在我们的第一次对话中，当你首次向我们的听众解释这一切时，莉萨，你曾告诉我，消除危害认定的努力，

sentences.en: and to fundamentally defang the legal framework behind how we regulate greenhouse gases, all of that had unfolded behind closed doors.
sentences.zh: 以及从根本上解除我们监管温室气体背后法律框架的武装，所有这些都是在闭门造车的情况下展开的。

sentences.en: It was very hard to understand how it had happened and who was involved in it.
sentences.zh: 很难理解这一切是如何发生的，又是谁参与其中。

sentences.en: But now, all these months later, you have reporting on what exactly that behind-the-scenes effort looked like and notably who was doing this behind-the-scenes work.
sentences.zh: 但现在，几个月过去了，你报道了幕后努力的具体情况，尤其是谁在做这些幕后工作。

sentences.en: So tell us about what you found.
sentences.zh: 所以给我们讲讲你发现了什么。

sentences.en: So it was pretty stunning to see how quickly and comprehensively the Trump administration moved to reverse the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 因此，看到特朗普政府以多快、多全面的速度采取行动推翻危害认定，真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: As soon as President Trump got into office, it was one of the early moves in January 2025 to tell the EPA to make a ruling on whether to reconsider this finding.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统刚一上台，就在2025年1月采取了早期行动之一，指示环保署就重新考虑这一认定作出裁决。

sentences.en: And what our reporting showed was this wasn't just an accident.
sentences.zh: 我们的报道显示，这绝非偶然。

sentences.en: This wasn't just years of persistence coming to fruition.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是多年的坚持终于有了结果。

sentences.en: That happens sometimes in Washington.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿，这种情况有时会发生。

sentences.en: This was made possible by a very small group of highly trained conservative lawyers who had spent years working in secret
sentences.zh: 这是由一小群受过高度训练的保守派律师促成的，他们花费数年时间在暗中工作，

sentences.en: to prepare for the moment when a Republican president could obliterate the government's ability to regulate climate change.
sentences.zh: 为共和党总统能够彻底摧毁政府监管气候变化能力的时刻做准备。

sentences.en: So who are these people, these conservative lawyers you're talking about?
sentences.zh: 那么这些人是谁，你谈到的这些保守派律师是谁？

sentences.en: It really starts with two people, Mandy Gunasekera and Jonathan Brightbilt.
sentences.zh: 这实际上始于两个人，曼迪·古纳塞卡拉和乔纳森·布赖特比尔。

sentences.en: The Green New Deal is not a serious proposal.
sentences.zh: 绿色新政绝不是一项严肃的提案。

sentences.en: It reads like Karl Marx's Christmas list and is a Soviet-style central planning document
sentences.zh: 它读起来就像卡尔·马克思的圣诞愿望清单，是一份苏联式的中央计划文件，

sentences.en: calling for a government takeover of the agricultural, transportation, housing, and health care sectors.
sentences.zh: 呼吁政府接管农业、交通、住房和医疗保健部门。

sentences.en: Gunasekera has a very long history fighting climate policies, not climate change, climate policies.
sentences.zh: 古纳塞卡拉在反对气候政策方面有着悠久的历史，不是气候变化，而是气候政策。

sentences.en: She used to work for Senator Jim Inhofe, who wrote a book called The Greatest Hoax, The Global Warming Conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 她过去曾为参议员吉姆·因霍夫工作，后者写过一本书，名为《最大的骗局：全球变暖的阴谋》。

sentences.en: In case we have forgotten, because we keep hearing that 2014 has been the warmest year on record,
sentences.zh: 如果我们忘记了，因为我们总是听到2014年是有记录以来最热的一年，

sentences.en: I asked the chair, you know what this is?
sentences.zh: 我问主席，你知道这是什么吗？

sentences.en: It's a snowball.
sentences.zh: 这是一个雪球。

sentences.en: And he one day threw a snowball on the Senate floor in February to prove that climate change was not a thing.
sentences.zh: 2月份的一天，他在参议院大厅扔了一个雪球，以证明气候变化根本不存在。

sentences.en: And that's just from outside here.
sentences.zh: 这只是外面传来的。

sentences.en: So it's very, very cold out, very unseasonal.
sentences.zh: 所以外面非常非常冷，很不合时节。

sentences.en: So here, Mr. President, catch this.
sentences.zh: 所以在这里，总统先生，接住这个。

sentences.en: Gunasekera is the aide who handed him that snowball, and that's one of the things she's pretty well known for in Washington.
sentences.zh: 古纳塞卡拉就是递给他那个雪球的助手，这也是她在华盛顿颇为出名的事情之一。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: She enters the first Trump administration, where she is instrumental in pushing for the United States to withdraw from the Paris Agreement, which President Trump eventually did.
sentences.zh: 她进入了第一届特朗普政府，在那里她在推动美国退出《巴黎协定》方面发挥了关键作用，特朗普总统最终退出了协定。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: During the Biden administration, she argued strenuously against policies that he put in place to reduce emissions from automobiles and power plants and the reSt.
sentences.zh: 在拜登政府期间，她极力反对他为减少汽车和发电厂等排放而实施的政策。

sentences.en: From day one, he's held true to that promise to, quote, shut down fossil fuel.
sentences.zh: 从第一天起，他就兑现了“关停化石燃料”的承诺。

sentences.en: And he and the Democrats have taken over 100 actions aimed at making it harder for oil and gas to be developed and delivered to market.
sentences.zh: 他和民主党人已经采取了100多项行动，旨在增加石油和天然气开发及投放市场的难度。

sentences.en: Essentially making the argument that policies to address climate change are more harmful than climate change itself.
sentences.zh: 基本观点是，应对气候变化的政策比气候变化本身更有害。

sentences.en: It's not climate change that farmers nor Americans should be worried about.
sentences.zh: 农民和美国人真正担心的不应该是气候变化。

sentences.en: It's the policies being pushed in the name of climate change that stand to do far much more damage.
sentences.zh: 而是以气候变化之名推行的政策，这些政策造成的破坏要大得多。

sentences.en: Her partner in trying to repeal the endangerment finding was an attorney named Jonathan Brightbill.
sentences.zh: 她试图废除危害认定的合作伙伴是一位名叫乔纳森·布赖特比尔的律师。

sentences.en: Before the Supreme Court will be the question of what limits exist in Clean Air Act Section 111D1.
sentences.zh: 摆在最高法院面前的将是《清洁空气法》第111条D款1项中存在哪些限制的问题。

sentences.en: He had served in the Justice Department under the first Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 他曾在第一届特朗普政府的司法部供职。

sentences.en: Everyone we have talked to has described him as a very sharp legal mind who really knows his way around the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act.
sentences.zh: 我们交谈过的每个人都形容他是一个思维极其敏锐的法律人才，对《清洁空气法》和《清洁水法》了如指掌。

sentences.en: The hinge issue can really succinctly be stated as follows.
sentences.zh: 核心问题可以简洁地表述如下。

sentences.en: Does EPA have the authority to determine the emissions rate based on what's achievable by what EPA thinks is the best system of emissions reduction, period?
sentences.zh: 环保署是否有权根据环保署认是的最佳减排系统可实现的目标来确定排放率？

sentences.en: And has made the argument in court that Democratic administrations have really overreached in their efforts to impose regulations to address climate change.
sentences.zh: 并在法庭上辩称，民主党政府在试图实施应对气候变化的法规时确实越权了。

sentences.en: He was essentially dealing with the downstream effects of the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在处理危害认定的下游效应。

sentences.en: And it makes your head swim to try and parse through the various clauses and instructions that are contained there.
sentences.zh: 试图仔细剖析其中包含的各种条款和指示，会让你头晕目眩。

sentences.en: Because of the endangerment finding, EPA has been dealing with a whiplash of regulations.
sentences.zh: 由于危害认定，环保署一直在应对如遭鞭笞般的法规变化。

sentences.en: They have been created in Democratic administrations, erased in Republican administrations, and fought in courts the entire time.
sentences.zh: 它们在民主党政府期间制定，在共和党政府期间废除，并在整个过程中在法庭上争斗不休。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Withdrawing the endangerment finding eliminates this situation entirely.
sentences.zh: 撤销危害认定完全消除了这种局面。

sentences.en: And that's what Gunasekara and Brightbill plotted to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是古纳塞卡拉和布赖特比尔策划要做的事情。

sentences.en: And how do they actually go about doing that?
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是怎么做到的呢？

sentences.en: So in the summer of 2022, Gunasekara and Brightbill start seeking funding for a big new project.
sentences.zh: 所以在2022年夏天，古纳塞卡拉和布赖特比尔开始为一个新的大型项目寻求资金。

sentences.en: They want to create a secret operation to kill the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 他们想建立一个秘密行动来消灭危害认定。

sentences.en: They pitched conservative organizations.
sentences.zh: 他们向保守派组织进行推销。

sentences.en: They asked for about $2 million for the ability to work on scientific studies and research from scientists who disagree with the mainstream science.
sentences.zh: 他们要求大约200万美元的资金，用于开展科学研究，并向那些不同意主流科学的科学家寻求研究支持。

sentences.en: They would start laying out the legal case for repealing the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 他们将开始为废除危害认定奠定法律基础。

sentences.en: All of these things were things that could be used by a next Republican president, they hoped, Donald Trump, on day one.
sentences.zh: 他们希望，所有这些都可以被下一任共和党总统——唐纳德·特朗普在第一天所利用。

sentences.en: They did eventually receive funding from a conservative organization, the Heritage Foundation.
sentences.zh: 他们最终确实从一个保守派组织传统基金会获得了资金。

sentences.en: The Heritage Foundation would go on to lead Project 2025, the blueprint for the next Republican president.
sentences.zh: 传统基金会后来领导了“2025计划”，即下一任共和党总统的蓝图。

sentences.en: And Mandy Gunasekara wrote the EPA chapter for Project 2025.
sentences.zh: 曼迪·古纳塞卡拉为“2025计划”撰写了环保署章节。

sentences.en: So these two lawyers, Gunasekara and Brightbill, they are ensuring that this cause of rolling back environmental regulations, of going after the endangerment finding,
sentences.zh: 因此，这两位律师古纳塞卡拉和布赖特比尔，他们正在确保撤销环境法规、追查危害认定的这项事业，

sentences.en: that it gets taken up by a major conservative think tank in Heritage with a ton of influence in Republican politics.
sentences.zh: 被传统基金会这样一个在共和党政治中具有巨大影响力的主要保守派智库所采纳。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Then in tandem, we have two other lawyers, much more high-profile figures, who are working in their own right to bring down the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 接着，我们还有另外两位律师，他们是更受瞩目的人物，他们也在以自己的方式努力推翻危害认定。

sentences.en: And who is that?
sentences.zh: 那是谁？

sentences.en: Russ Vogt and Jeff Clark.
sentences.zh: 罗斯·沃格特和杰夫·克拉克。

sentences.en: Much better known.
sentences.zh: 知名度更高。

sentences.en: Much better known figures.
sentences.zh: 知名度更高的人物。

sentences.en: Russell Vogt, as we know, during the Biden years, starts a think tank of his own, the Center for Renewing America, where they were keeping the MAGA movement alive.
sentences.zh: 如我们所知，在拜登执政期间，拉塞尔·沃格特创办了自己的智库——革新美国中心，他们在那里让MAGA运动保持活力。

sentences.en: Jeff Clark has been in the fight against the endangerment finding for decades.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·克拉克几十年来一直参与反对危害认定的斗争。

sentences.en: EPA, it seems to me, is too big.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，环保署太大了。

sentences.en: It's bloated on stimulus money.
sentences.zh: 它因刺激资金而膨胀。

sentences.en: And it seems hell-bent on expansion.
sentences.zh: 而且它似乎铁了心要扩张。

sentences.en: Before there ever was an endangerment finding, he went to court to argue that the EPA doesn't have and shouldn't have the legal authority to address greenhouse gases.
sentences.zh: 早在出现危害认定之前，他就去法院辩称环保署没有也本不该拥有解决温室气体的法律权力。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter to EPA if it's absurd, if its regulations are going to lead to absurd consequences that inflict massive harm on the national economy.
sentences.zh: 环保署才不管它是否荒谬，不管其法规是否会导致对国民经济造成巨大伤害的荒谬后果。

sentences.en: He loses that.
sentences.zh: 他输了。

sentences.en: And that, from everything we have been told, is really a motivating factor for years with Jeff Clark, what he sees as righting a wrong.
sentences.zh: 根据我们所听到的一切，这确实是杰夫·克拉克多年来的一个强烈动机，他认为这是在纠正错误。

sentences.en: Of course, the other thing Jeff Clark is known for, and I think a lot of our listeners will remember this, is that at the end of the first Trump term,
sentences.zh: 当然，杰夫·克拉克的另一件为人所知的事情，我想我们的很多听众都会记得，是在第一届特朗普政府行将结束时，

sentences.en: he emerges from deep within the Justice Department as an ally of President Trump in trying to overturn the 2020 election,
sentences.zh: 他从司法部深处脱颖而出，成为特朗普总统推翻2020年大选的盟友，

sentences.en: so much so that Trump briefly considers making him the acting Attorney General.
sentences.zh: 以至于特朗普一度考虑让他担任代理司法部长。

sentences.en: And that so scares people at the Department of Justice that many of them threaten to quit.
sentences.zh: 这把司法部的人吓坏了，以至于许多人威胁要辞职。

sentences.en: If it happens, President backs down.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，总统就会退缩。

sentences.en: But Clark becomes known as a major election denier.
sentences.zh: 但克拉克成了著名的选举否定论者。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Sure enough, President Trump wins the presidency.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，特朗普总统赢得了总统大选。

sentences.en: Three out of four of the people that we're talking about here, Bright, Bill, Clark, and Vogt,
sentences.zh: 我们在这里谈论的四个人中的三个，布赖特比尔、克拉克和沃格特，

sentences.en: go back into the administration and are able to hand the president a very clear roadmap for the biggest climate deregulation in American history.
sentences.zh: 重新进入政府，并能够向总统提供一份非常清晰的路线图，以实施美国历史上规模最大的气候放松管制。

sentences.en: And that's what's being followed right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前正在遵循的做法。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, Lisa, once a bunch of these advocates of repealing the endangerment finding end up inside the White House and in a position to actually repeal it, what's the technical case,
sentences.zh: 那么，莉萨，一旦这群废除危害认定的倡导者最终进入白宫并处于实际废除它的位置，他们的技术理由是什么，

sentences.en: what's the legal case that they make to try to do that?
sentences.zh: 他们提出的试图这样做的法律理由是什么？

sentences.en: So, remember I told you that the Obama administration wrote the endangerment finding because the Supreme Court said, in order to regulate these gases,
sentences.zh: 所以，还记得我告诉过你奥巴马政府写了危害认定是因为最高法院说过，为了监管这些气体，

sentences.en: you need to determine that these are harmful to human health and the environment.
sentences.zh: 你需要确定这些对人类健康和环境有害。

sentences.en: So, now this administration, the Trump administration, is looking at that finding and they're saying, the science that you used is something we don't agree with.
sentences.zh: 所以现在本届政府，即特朗普政府，正在审视那项认定，他们说，你们使用的科学是我们不同意的。

sentences.en: And they're saying the legal rationale is problematic.
sentences.zh: 他们说法律依据是有问题的。

sentences.en: So, start with the science.
sentences.zh: 所以，从科学开始。

sentences.en: So, they have made the case that the predictions that were made about the impacts of climate change back in 2009 were too pessimistic.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们提出了一种情况，即2009年对气候变化影响的预测过于悲观。

sentences.en: Their evidence to support that claim is a report that five handpicked climate contrarians wrote in secret for the Department of Energy last year.
sentences.zh: 他们支持这一说法的证据是，去年五位精选的气候异见人士为能源部秘密撰写的一份报告。

sentences.en: It was designed to support the repeal of the endangerment finding and, no surprise to anyone, the conclusion was that climate change threats have been overblown.
sentences.zh: 它旨在支持废除危害认定，不出任何人所料，其结论是气候变化威胁被夸大了。

sentences.en: And what multitudes of scientists have told us are two things.
sentences.zh: 广大科学家告诉我们的主要有两点。

sentences.en: Yeah, the planet is better off than what was predicted in 2009 because the international community has acted, not enough, not fast enough,
sentences.zh: 是的，地球比2009年预测的要好，因为国际社会采取了行动，虽然不够，速度也不够快，

sentences.en: but has done work towards reducing emissions.
sentences.zh: 但确实在减少排放方面做了工作。

sentences.en: But what's also true is that every bit of emissions that enters the atmosphere leads to more warming, which leads to more health impacts.
sentences.zh: 但同样真实的是，进入大气层的每一点排放都会导致更多的变暖，从而导致更多对健康的影响。

sentences.en: And all of the things that we know continue to endanger human health and the environment.
sentences.zh: 以及我们所知道的继续危及人类健康和环境的所有事情。

sentences.en: Scientists say that that research is even more ironclad today than it was in 2009.
sentences.zh: 科学家表示，今天这项研究甚至比2009年时更具铁证。

sentences.en: Then there's the Trump administration's legal arguments for repealing the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 然后是特朗普政府废除危害认定的法律论据。

sentences.en: There's a couple.
sentences.zh: 这里有一对。

sentences.en: Take a step back.
sentences.zh: 退后一步。

sentences.en: The endangerment finding, that flowed from a law, the 1970 Clean Air Act.
sentences.zh: 关于温室气体危害认定，它源于一部法律，即1970年的《清洁空气法》。

sentences.en: But this EPA is arguing that the Clean Air Act only allows EPA to regulate what it calls local and regional pollutants.
sentences.zh: 但现任环保局辩称，《清洁空气法》只允许环保局监管其所谓的本地和区域污染物。

sentences.en: Things like soot from industrial sources, factories, power plants, stuff that's really bad when you breathe it in.
sentences.zh: 比如工业源产生的煤烟、工厂、发电厂排放的物质，这些吸入体内会带来极大的危害。

sentences.en: Greenhouse gas emissions don't work that way.
sentences.zh: 温室气体排放并非如此。

sentences.en: Carbon dioxide, methane, you know, all these gases, they disperse into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 二氧化碳、甲烷，你知道的，所有这些气体都会弥散到大气中。

sentences.en: They trap heat, they linger from decades to centuries, and alter the climate.
sentences.zh: 它们会锁住热量，留存几十年到几个世纪，并改变气候。

sentences.en: So this EPA is making the argument that it just does not have the legal authority to deal with those kinds of, let's call them global pollutants.
sentences.zh: 因此，现任环保局提出的论点是，它根本不具备处理此类（我们不妨称之为全球污染物）的法律权限。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So their argument is that the endangerment finding misunderstands the Clean Air Act and thinks that you can regulate greenhouse gases that, by definition, are not local.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的观点是，危害认定误解了《清洁空气法》，并且认为你可以监管那些按定义来说并非局部的温室气体。

sentences.en: They end up in the sky.
sentences.zh: 它们最终会进入天空。

sentences.en: They end up far from their original source.
sentences.zh: 它们最终会飘到远离最初源头的地方。

sentences.en: And therefore, the endangerment finding is not legally sound.
sentences.zh: 因此，危害认定在法律上是站不住脚的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Do lawyers agree with that argument?
sentences.zh: 律师们认同这种说法吗？

sentences.en: They're mixed.
sentences.zh: 意见不一。

sentences.en: I mean, there are some conservative lawyers who think that the EPA has a really good case to make.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些保守派律师认为环保局确实握有很好的论据。

sentences.en: You know, environmental attorneys that we've spoken to have said that the George W.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们交谈过的环境法律师表示，小布什

sentences.en: Bush administration made similar arguments to defend its decision not to issue an endangerment finding and loSt.
sentences.zh: 政府曾提出类似论点来为其不发布危害认定的决定进行辩护，并且败诉了。

sentences.en: But there's another argument that's linked.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个与之相关的论点。

sentences.en: Since 2009, the Supreme Court has repeatedly ruled against environmental regulations that require big transformational changes to industry and the economy.
sentences.zh: 自2009年以来，最高法院多次作出不利于环保法规的裁决，这些法规要求对工业和经济进行大规模的根本性变革。

sentences.en: And so the Trump administration is saying, based on that new legal landscape and the fact that so many of the regulations that have stemmed from the endangerment finding require,
sentences.zh: 因此特朗普政府表示，基于这一新的法律格局以及源自危害认定的诸多法规，在他们看来

sentences.en: in their view, sweeping technology, economic changes, they're arguing that the source, the endangerment finding, should be overturned.
sentences.zh: 需要进行深刻的技术和经济变革，他们主张推翻这一源头，即危害认定。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: If so many regulations that flow from the endangerment finding eventually get struck down by the Supreme Court, then the fruit of those regulations, the finding itself,
sentences.zh: 如果源自危害认定的那么多法规最终都被最高法院推翻，那么这些法规的果实，即认定本身，

sentences.en: should itself be seen as illegal.
sentences.zh: 本身也应该被视为非法的。

sentences.en: Unless Congress explicitly gives the EPA authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions, which, after decades, they have never done.
sentences.zh: 除非国会明确赋予环保局监管温室气体排放的权力，而几十年来，国会从未这样做过。

sentences.en: And this Congress is very unlikely to ever give it that power.
sentences.zh: 而且这一届国会也极不可能赋予其这种权力。

sentences.en: Definitely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不可能。

sentences.en: Okay, so now that we understand the Trump administration's arguments here, just explain how they're going to turn those arguments into the end of the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 好的，既然我们已经理解了特朗普政府在此处的论点，请解释一下他们将如何把这些论点转化为终结危害认定的手段。

sentences.en: What do we expect the administration to do to end the finding?
sentences.zh: 我们预计政府会采取什么行动来终结这一认定？

sentences.en: So what we expect is, on Thursday, the administrator of the EPA, Lee Zeldin, who has said that he plans to drive a dagger through the heart of the climate change religion,
sentences.zh: 所以我们预计，在周四，环保局局长李·泽尔丁——他曾表示计划“给气候变化宗教的心脏插上一把匕首”——

sentences.en: his words, will announce the end of the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 用他的话来说，将宣布危害认定的终结。

sentences.en: But it's not the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 但这并非故事的结局。

sentences.en: Meaning?
sentences.zh: 什么意思？

sentences.en: Environmental groups, states, are going to immediately sue.
sentences.zh: 环保组织和各州将立即提起诉讼。

sentences.en: And this will be played out in the courts over the next several years.
sentences.zh: 这将在未来几年内在法庭上展开较量。

sentences.en: And what do we expect will happen in the courts?
sentences.zh: 我们预计法庭上会发生什么？

sentences.en: And just how high up in the courts is this likely to go?
sentences.zh: 这桩官司预计会打到多高的法院级别？

sentences.en: Well, that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关键就在这里。

sentences.en: We know what the group that we've been talking about, the folks who laid out this roadmap, hope to see.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们一直在讨论的那个群体，即制定了这个路线图的人，他们希望能看到什么。

sentences.en: And that is that this case gets before the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 那就是这个案子能够上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: And if that happens, there is a lot of hope in the conservative movement that the landmark climate change case, Massachusetts versus EPA,
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，保守派阵营中抱有很大希望，即具有里程碑意义的气候变化案——马萨诸塞州诉环保局案——

sentences.en: could be overturned or significantly weakened.
sentences.zh: 可能会被推翻或大大削弱。

sentences.en: So their hope is that the endangerment finding ends up before the Supreme Court in such a way that a conservative majority of the Supreme Court would overturn the original Supreme Court ruling that allows the endangerment finding to have ever come into existence.
sentences.zh: 因此他们的希望是，危害认定最终呈现在最高法院面前的方式，能够让最高法院的保守派多数推翻最初允许危害认定得以诞生的最高法院裁决。

sentences.en: You hit the nail on the head.
sentences.zh: 你一针见血。

sentences.en: And if that happens, a future president would not be able to reinstate regulations addressing greenhouse gas emissions unless and until Congress explicitly said, go do that.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，未来的总统将无法恢复旨在应对温室气体排放的法规，除非且直到国会明确表示：去这么做吧。

sentences.en: And let's presume for just a moment, Lisa, that our legal system does allow the endangerment finding to go away.
sentences.zh: 让我们暂时假设，丽莎，我们的法律系统确实允许危害认定消失。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the repercussions of that on the environment, on industry,
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈这对环境、对工业所产生的反响，

sentences.en: and let's just start with the impact on industry that now operates under these regulations that I presume suddenly would start to go away.
sentences.zh: 我们先从对目前在这些法规下运作的工业的影响谈起，我猜这些法规很快就会开始消失。

sentences.en: Well, one thing that industry would get is the certainty that it has said it always wants, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，工业将得到的一点是它一直声称想要的确定性，对吧？

sentences.en: It would know that it would not face what has been a decade and a half of whiplash.
sentences.zh: 它会知道自己将不再面对长达十五年的政策急转弯。

sentences.en: Democrats come in and start to regulate power plants and automobiles and the rest, and then a Republican administration comes in and removes or weakens them.
sentences.zh: 民主党上台开始监管发电厂和汽车及其他行业，然后共和党政府上台又将其取消或削弱。

sentences.en: There would be a new playing field, and it would not include regulatory restrictions.
sentences.zh: 将会出现一个新的竞技场，并且其中将不包含监管限制。

sentences.en: So the question is, will this lead to industries polluting more?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，这会导致各行业污染更严重吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And yeah, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我们并不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, it is certainly possible that because companies have already put billions of dollars into clean technology, whether it's for EVs or pollution controls in power plants,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，完全有可能的是，由于企业已经在清洁技术上投入了数十亿美元，无论是用于电动汽车还是发电厂的污染治理，

sentences.en: that they will continue to do so.
sentences.zh: 它们仍将继续这样做。

sentences.en: There's also public pressure, and companies very much care about how they are seen and whether they are stepping up to a challenge like climate change.
sentences.zh: 还有公众压力，企业非常关心自己如何被看待，以及它们是否在迎接气候变化这样的挑战。

sentences.en: But the reality is, left completely unshackled, as the CPA is about to do, we don't really know how industry will react.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，如果完全不受束缚，正如环保局即将做的那样，我们真的不知道行业会作何反应。

sentences.en: Well, given that uncertainty, what would the elimination of the endangerment finding mean for the environment and for climate change writ large?
sentences.zh: 嗯，鉴于这种不确定性，取消危害认定对环境和广义上的气候变化意味着什么？

sentences.en: Is that suddenly now pretty much in the hands of industry?
sentences.zh: 难道现在这突然几乎完全掌握在工业手中了吗？

sentences.en: It's such a hard question to answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个太难回答的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, yes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的。

sentences.en: And part of the reason why is that the Trump administration has already pretty effectively restricted some of the things that states can do to address climate change on their own.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，特朗普政府已经相当有效地限制了各州为应对气候变化而能够自主采取的一些措施。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: California is the only state in the country that can set more stringent environmental regulations than the federal government.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州是全国唯一一个可以制定比联邦政府更严格的环境法规的州。

sentences.en: It needs a waiver to do that.
sentences.zh: 它需要获得豁免权才能这样做。

sentences.en: California tried to set even stricter automobile emissions rules.
sentences.zh: 加州曾试图制定更严格的汽车排放规则。

sentences.en: They had a plan to eliminate the sales of combustion engine vehicles, you know, in the next decade or so.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个计划，要在未来十年左右淘汰燃油车的销售，你知道的。

sentences.en: But the Trump administration and Congress rescinded that waiver.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普政府和国会撤销了该豁免权。

sentences.en: I can't see California getting another waiver, at least during the next three years.
sentences.zh: 我看不出加州在未来三年内还能再次获得豁免。

sentences.en: So that really ties the hands of not just California, but other like-minded states that might want to do something very ambitious on automobiles.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实束缚了不仅仅是加州的手脚，也束缚了其他志同道合、可能想在汽车领域采取雄心勃勃行动的州的手脚。

sentences.en: So in the absence of major new state regulation and a federal government that doesn't want to regulate most of these greenhouse emissions at all,
sentences.zh: 因此，在缺乏重大的州级新法规以及一个根本不想监管绝大多数温室气体排放的联邦政府的情况下，

sentences.en: what do scientists say that the world starts to look like?
sentences.zh: 科学家们说世界将会变成什么样子？

sentences.en: Scientists are worried.
sentences.zh: 科学家们很担忧。

sentences.en: I mean, the United States is the largest historic emitter of climate change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国是气候变化历史上的最大排放国。

sentences.en: It's the second largest annual emitter of carbon pollution and greenhouse gases.
sentences.zh: 它是碳污染和温室气体的第二大年度排放国。

sentences.en: If the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果美国

sentences.en: is not doing its part, a lot of countries could start to wonder, why should they?
sentences.zh: 没有做好自己的本分，许多国家可能会开始纳闷：凭什么它们要这样做？

sentences.en: And the most important is China.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的就是中国。

sentences.en: And that's the big fear that a lot have relayed to me.
sentences.zh: 这就是许多人向我传达的巨大担忧。

sentences.en: If the United States is successful in not just failing to reduce its own emissions, but convincing other countries that they don't need to either,
sentences.zh: 如果美国不仅没能成功减少自身的排放，还成功说服其他国家它们也无需这样做，

sentences.en: scientists feel that could have a really dangerous domino effect for the planet.
sentences.zh: 科学家们认为这可能会对地球产生极其危险的多米诺骨牌效应。

sentences.en: And where do those dominoes eventually fall?
sentences.zh: 这些多米诺骨牌最终会倒向哪里？

sentences.en: I mean, they fall in more severe rising temperatures and more droughts and hotter droughts,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们倒向更严重的升温、更多的干旱以及更炎热的干旱，

sentences.en: more frequent and severe wildfires, rising sea levels from melting glaciers that are threatening coastal communities.
sentences.zh: 更加频繁和严重的野火，以及融化的冰川导致海平面上升，从而威胁到沿海社区。

sentences.en: These kinds of changes also directly damage human health, scientists tell us.
sentences.zh: 科学家告诉我们，这类变化还会直接损害人类健康。

sentences.en: They damage food security, water supplies.
sentences.zh: 它们会损害粮食安全、水资源供应。

sentences.en: They lead to an increase in vector-borne diseases, Lyme disease, dengue.
sentences.zh: 它们会导致虫媒传染病增加，如莱姆病、登革热。

sentences.en: Anyway, there's a whole sweeping landscape of impacts that scientists are warning will get worse if emissions continue to go up.
sentences.zh: 总之，如果排放量继续上升，科学家警告说，将会有一整片广泛的影响景观变得更加恶劣。

sentences.en: I feel like what's quite remarkable about the story that you've told here is how quickly this country's relationship to
sentences.zh: 我觉得你所讲述的故事中非常引人注目的一点是，这个国家与

sentences.en: greenhouse gases, the idea that they create climate change and that this is something to be addressed by the government,
sentences.zh: 温室气体的关系、关于它们造成气候变化以及这应该由政府来解决的这种观念，

sentences.en: how quickly, really just in a decade and a half, that's changed.
sentences.zh: 转变是如此之快，真的仅仅在十五年里就变了。

sentences.en: If you go back to the mid-early 2000s, when the endangerment finding was written,
sentences.zh: 如果你回到2000年代中前期，也就是撰写危害认定的时候，

sentences.en: it seemed like much of the business and even political world was starting to become aligned in this sense that there was a problem and that something could be done about it.
sentences.zh: 似乎很大一部分商业界甚至政治界开始达成共识，即这是一个问题，并且有些事情是可以为此做的。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Nancy Pelosi, lifelong Democrat and Speaker of the House.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是南希·佩洛西，终身民主党人兼众议院议长。

sentences.en: And I'm Newt Gingrich, lifelong Republican, and I used to be Speaker.
sentences.zh: 我是纽特·金里奇，终身共和党人，我曾担任过议长。

sentences.en: I'm sure you remember the famous ad where Nancy Pelosi and Newt Gingrich were sitting on a couch together in front of the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 我确信你还记得那则著名的广告，南希·佩洛西和纽特·金里奇并肩坐在国会大厦前的沙发上。

sentences.en: We don't always see eye to eye, do we, Newt?
sentences.zh: 我们并非总是意见一致，对吧，纽特？

sentences.en: No, but we do agree our country must take action to address climate change.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我们确实同意我们的国家必须采取行动应对气候变化。

sentences.en: And there wasn't always going to be ever, of course, agreement about what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 当然，对于究竟该采取什么行动，并不总是能一直达成共识。

sentences.en: Businesses weren't thrilled about some of the costs entailed in changing their conduct.
sentences.zh: 企业对于改变行为所带来的部分成本并不感到兴奋。

sentences.en: But a lot of people got on board with the idea that something needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 但许多人赞同必须采取行动的这一理念。

sentences.en: And yet, as you've explained here,
sentences.zh: 然而，正如你在这里所解释的，

sentences.en: a very persistent group of ideologically aligned climate change skeptics kept at it through Republican and Democratic presidencies and have succeeded in making their view,
sentences.zh: 一小群立场坚定、意识形态一致的气候变化怀疑论者，在共和党和民主党执政期间一直坚持不懈，并成功将他们的观点——

sentences.en: which isn't necessarily the nation's view, become the government's official policy.
sentences.zh: 这未必是全国的观点——变成了政府的官方政策。

sentences.en: And that's something to behold.
sentences.zh: 这真是一件令人瞩目的事情。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And one of the things that became clear as we were reporting this story out is that this group of conservative lawyers, their views on climate change were not in the mainstream,
sentences.zh: 在我们报道这个故事的过程中，有一点变得清晰起来，那就是这群保守派律师，他们对气候变化的观点并不属于主流，

sentences.en: even of their own party.
sentences.zh: 甚至在他们自己的党内也是如此。

sentences.en: But they were persistent and they did an enormous amount of planning.
sentences.zh: 但他们坚持不懈，并做了大量的规划工作。

sentences.en: And that persistence paid off in the form of President Trump, who, you know, we all know his views on climate change, calls it a hoax, calls it a scam.
sentences.zh: 这种坚持得到了回报，化身为了特朗普总统，你知道的，我们都知道他对气候变化的看法，他称之为骗局，称之为圈套。

sentences.en: And when President Trump was elected, these two forces joined and they were ready to get this anti-climate agenda done.
sentences.zh: 当特朗普总统当选时，这两股力量合流了，他们准备好将这套反气候议程付诸实施。

sentences.en: And later today, when the endangerment finding is repealed, it will be, in the words of one climate contrarian, total victory for their cause.
sentences.zh: 今天晚些时候，当危害认定被废除时，用一位气候异见人士的话来说，这将是他们事业的彻底胜利。

sentences.en: Well, Lisa, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，丽莎，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the mystery surrounding the federal government's decision to abruptly shut down the airspace around El Paso, Texas, originally for 10 days, appeared to be solved.
sentences.zh: 周三，围绕联邦政府突然决定关闭德克萨斯州埃尔帕索周边领空（最初为期10天）的谜团，似乎得到了解开。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the closure was announced after officials from U.S.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，此次关闭是在美国

sentences.en: Customs and Border Protection decided to try out a new anti-drone laser technology in order to shoot at what they believed was a drone from Mexican drug cartels.
sentences.zh: 海关与边境保护局官员决定试用一种新的反无人机激光技术，以向他们认为是来自墨西哥贩毒集团的无人机开火之后宣布的。

sentences.en: But the border protection officials failed to give officials from the Federal Aviation Administration enough time to assess the risks of the new technology on commercial planes.
sentences.zh: 但边境保护官员未能给联邦航空管理局的官员足够的时间来评估新技术对商业飞机的风险。

sentences.en: That prompted the FAA to shut down the airspace before quickly reversing their own decision.
sentences.zh: 这促使联邦航空管理局下令关闭领空，随后又迅速撤销了自己的决定。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 而且

sentences.en: How many of Epstein's co-conspirators have you indicted?
sentences.zh: 你起诉了爱泼斯坦的多少同谋？

sentences.en: How many perpetrators are you even investigating?
sentences.zh: 你甚至在调查多少名施害者？

sentences.en: First, you showed a—I find a—
sentences.zh: 首先，你展示了一个——我发现一个——

sentences.en: How many have you indicted?
sentences.zh: 你起诉了多少人？

sentences.en: Excuse me.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: I'm going to answer the question.
sentences.zh: 我要回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Answer my question.
sentences.zh: 回答我的问题。

sentences.en: No, I'm going to answer the question the way I want to answer the question you're doing.
sentences.zh: 不，我要以我想要回答你正在提问的方式来回答问题。

sentences.en: During a combative hearing on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 在周三一场火药味十足的听证会上，

sentences.en: Democratic members of Congress sharply criticized Attorney General Pam Bondi for her department's handling of documents related to Jeffrey Epstein and her repeated efforts to prosecute enemies of the president.
sentences.zh: 国会民主党成员严厉批评了司法部长帕姆·邦迪，指责其部门对杰弗里·爱泼斯坦相关文件的处理不当，以及她屡次试图起诉总统政敌的行为。

sentences.en: You've turned the people's department of justice into Trump's instrument of revenge.
sentences.zh: 你把人民的司法部变成了特朗普的复仇工具。

sentences.en: Trump orders up prosecutions like pizza, and you deliver every time.
sentences.zh: 特朗普像点披萨一样下达起诉指令，而你每次都照办。

sentences.en: He tells you to go after James Comey, Letitia James, Lisa—
sentences.zh: 他叫你去对付詹姆斯·科米、莱蒂蒂亚·詹姆斯、丽莎——

sentences.en: Bondi forcefully defended her actions, frequently interrupted lawmakers, and at times insulted them,
sentences.zh: 邦迪有力地为自己的行为辩护，频频打断议员讲话，有时甚至出言侮辱，

sentences.en: as she did to Representative Jamie Raskin of Maryland when he instructed Bondi to stop filibustering in response to questions from Democrats.
sentences.zh: 就像她对待马里兰州众议员杰米·拉斯金那样，当时拉斯金指示邦迪停止在回答民主党问题时进行冗长诡辩。

sentences.en: And I told you about that, Attorney General, before you started— You don't tell me anything.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说过这个了，司法部长，在你开始之前—— 你什么也没跟我说。

sentences.en: Yeah, oh, I did tell you because we saw what you did in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 是的，哦，我的确跟你说过了，因为我们看到了你在参议院的表现。

sentences.en: You're a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 你是个律师。

sentences.en: Not even a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 连律师都不是。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll be in order.
sentences.zh: 大家也许该安静一下了。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Eric Krupke, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Anna Foley.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由埃里克·克鲁普克、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和安娜·弗利制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Maria Byrne and Devin Taylor.
sentences.zh: 由玛丽亚·伯恩和德文·泰勒剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains music by Aliciava Etude, Marion Lozano, and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 包含由阿莉西亚瓦·埃蒂德、马里昂·洛萨诺和丹·鲍威尔创作的音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》就到这里。

sentences.en: I'm Michael O'Bara.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·奥巴拉。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人热血沸腾的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》节目中，由我萨拉·凯尼格为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
